security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown examples, configuration names, or visible Localhero.ai documentation links. The real risks are expected networked CLI execution, broad Localhero CLI command scope, and API-key handling guidance that could expose secrets. No prompt injection or malicious exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the exact subcommands required by the workflow, and require explicit user confirmation for push, pull, clone, force, and prune operations.

remediation.issue: API key shown as a command-line argument
remediation.suggestion: Prefer interactive login, environment variables, or secret managers, and warn users not to paste real API keys into prompts or shell history.

remediation.issue: Networked translation commands can change files
remediation.suggestion: Tell users before running translate, push, pull, clone, or ci commands, then summarize changed files and remote actions afterward.

content.value_statement: Translation work often breaks when source strings, glossary terms, and target files drift apart. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code update source strings and use Localhero.ai workflows consistently.
actual_capabilities: Reads localhero.json to identify source locale and translation file paths.
Adds or updates source-language i18n keys for JSON, YAML, PO, and POT workflows.
Runs changed-key translation through the Localhero CLI when no GitHub Action handles it.
Retrieves glossary terms and project tone settings through the Localhero CLI.
Guides users to the Localhero.ai web UI for translation review and project settings.
limitations: Requires an authenticated Localhero.ai CLI setup before translation commands can run.
Uses networked Localhero.ai services and may modify local translation files.
Does not manually translate target locales when Localhero.ai handles them.
Cannot verify translation quality beyond available glossary and project settings.

use_cases.title: Add Localized UI Copy
use_cases.description: Add new source strings for buttons, forms, alerts, and page headings while matching existing key naming patterns.

use_cases.title: Keep Product Language Consistent
use_cases.description: Use glossary terms and project tone settings before writing user-facing copy for a new feature.

use_cases.title: Prepare Translation Updates for Review
use_cases.description: Generate changed translations and summarize the source keys that should be reviewed in Localhero.ai.

prompt_templates.title: Add One String
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for a small UI update.
prompt_templates.prompt: Add a source string for the new settings save button. Follow the existing key naming style and update only the source locale file.

prompt_templates.title: Update Feature Copy
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task for a feature with several user-facing strings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the onboarding screen and add missing source strings. Use the project glossary before writing copy and keep the tone consistent.

prompt_templates.title: Generate Changed Translations
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate task after source strings have changed.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the Localhero configuration, confirm whether the GitHub Action handles translations, and run changed-key translation only when needed.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Localization Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this branch for new user-facing text, add missing source keys, refresh glossary and settings context, and summarize translation changes for review.

output_examples.input: Add a success message for password reset.
output_examples.output: A source-locale message is added under the existing account message area. Changed translations are generated only if the project needs a CLI run.

output_examples.input: Review checkout copy for glossary consistency.
output: Glossary terms are checked before copy changes are made.
Checkout source strings are updated to match the project voice.
The final response lists changed source messages for reviewer attention.

output_examples.input: Prepare this branch for localization review.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies source string changes, runs the appropriate Localhero workflow, and points reviewers to the Localhero.ai review surface.

best_practices: Add or edit source locale strings first, then let Localhero.ai manage target translations.
Review glossary and project settings before writing public product copy.
Use changed-key translation for smaller diffs when a GitHub Action is not handling translations.
anti_patterns: Do not edit generated target translations manually unless the project workflow requires it.
Do not paste real API keys into prompts, examples, or command history.
Do not run push, pull, clone, force, or prune commands without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps manage source-language i18n strings and Localhero.ai translation workflows inside coding assistants.

faq.question: Does it translate text itself?
faq.answer: No. It writes source strings and uses Localhero.ai or the configured GitHub Action for target translations.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: A project needs localhero.json and an authenticated Localhero.ai CLI or GitHub Action workflow.

faq.question: Can it use glossary terms?
faq.answer: Yes. It can request glossary and project settings through the Localhero CLI before writing copy.

faq.question: What should users review?
faq.answer: Users should review changed source strings, generated translations, and any CLI actions that modify files or remote state.
